issues.description: The Stock.take(...) method has inconsistent return types across artifacts: the problem statement UML specifies take(String): int and the reference solution implements take(...) returning int (returning -1 on failure and new quantity on success), but the template implementation declares take(String): boolean. This mismatch will cause compile errors or confusion when students implement SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() and other logic that expect an int return value (e.g., checking for -1 to detect failure).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.take(String) signature match the specification and solution by changing its return type from boolean to int. Implement it to return -1 when the ingredient doesn't exist or quantity is insufficient, and otherwise decrement the quantity and return the new quantity. Alternatively, if boolean semantics are intended, update the problem statement and solution to use boolean consistently; however, aligning the template to the UML/solution (int) is recommended to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution implementation define Stock.take(String) to return an int (using -1 to indicate missing/unavailable ingredient), but the template repository implements Stock.take(String) as returning a boolean (true/false). This mismatch in the method's return type/contract creates a semantic mapping barrier: students following the problem text or the solution will expect an int sentinel (-1) to indicate failure and use that in SealSaloon.checkOrderReady, while the template's boolean signature forces a different usage pattern and may confuse students about how to detect unavailable ingredients.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by changing Stock.take(String) to return an int. Implement it to return -1 when the ingredient is missing or quantity < 1, otherwise decrement the quantity and return the new quantity (as shown in the solution). Update any comments or usages in the template to reflect the int return contract.
